intervals.label: operation (ALPHA 1 from 2005, ALPHA 2 from 2012, ALPHA-g and ALPHA 3 from 2021)
intervals.note: Start year from the official hardware list ("ALPHA 1 (2005– 2012)") and CERN ("Set up in late 2005"). End: 31 August 2026, when the Antimatter Factory fell silent for Long Shutdown 3. the CERN Courier of 17 August 2000 reports the AD "coming into action for physics" and supplying ATRAP, ATHENA and ASACUSA

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (no antiproton beam)
intervals.note: The Antimatter Factory (AD and ELENA) delivered its last beams on 31 August 2026 and "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages" (CERN, 31 August 2026); no experiment-specific restart date is published, so the end is left open.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

placements.note: ALPHA 1 (2005–2012) sat on the same AD experimental floor but the official page names no hall; campus-grade site used for all ALPHA apparatus.

summary.plain: The horizontal ALPHA traps in which antihydrogen atoms are made, held in a magnetic bottle and illuminated with lasers and microwaves.
summary.technical: ALPHA 1 (2005-2012), ALPHA 2 (2012-) and ALPHA 3 (2021-): Penning-Malmberg traps for antihydrogen synthesis with a superposed neutral-atom minimum-B trap, laser access for spectroscopy and laser cooling.

technology.quote: Catching trap introduced to split functionality away from antihydrogen region to improve mechanical access (for e.g. lasers).
technology.value: Octupole minimum-B neutral-atom trap superposed on a Penning-Malmberg trap for antihydrogen synthesis, with a catching trap and laser access (ALPHA 2/3)
